personal-injury.lead: Most injury claims must be filed within two years, a person more than 50% at fault recovers nothing, and car crash injuries start with your own PIP insurance.
rows: 2 years for negligence claims that arose on or after March 24, 2023 (Fla. Stat. § 95.11)
More than 50% at fault: no recovery; 50% or less: damages reduced by your share (Fla. Stat. § 768.81)
Your own PIP pays first, up to $10,000, if you get care within 14 days (Fla. Stat. § 627.736)
Contingency fees are capped, for example 33⅓% of the first $1 million if the case resolves before the defendant answers (Rule 4-1.5)
Claims above $50,000 go to the circuit court; smaller claims go to the county court
faq: How long do I have to file a personal injury lawsuit in Florida?

Two years from the date of the injury for most negligence claims that arose on or after March 24, 2023. Claims that arose before that date have four years. Medical malpractice and wrongful death claims also have two-year deadlines, with their own rules on when the clock starts.
Can I recover compensation if I was partly at fault?
Yes, if you were 50% or less at fault; your damages are reduced by your share. If you are found more than 50% at fault, Florida law bars recovery, except in medical negligence cases.
How much does a personal injury lawyer cost in Florida?

Most work on a contingency fee: a percentage of the recovery and nothing if there is none. Florida caps these fees, for example at 33⅓% of the first $1 million if the case resolves before the defendant answers the lawsuit, and 40% after that. You can cancel the agreement within 3 business days of signing.
Who pays my medical bills after a car accident in Florida?

Your own Personal Injury Protection (PIP) insurance pays first, whoever caused the crash: 80% of medical bills and 60% of lost income, up to $10,000 combined, if you get care within 14 days. You can claim against the at-fault driver only for serious, permanent injuries.

criminal-defense.lead: Florida sets deadlines for charging a crime, and anyone who cannot afford a lawyer is entitled to a public defender.
rows: Time limit to prosecute a first-degree felony
Capital and life felonies and felonies resulting in death (§ 775.15)
faq: How long does Florida have to charge a crime?

Generally 4 years for a first-degree felony, 3 years for other felonies, 2 years for a first-degree misdemeanor and 1 year for a second-degree misdemeanor. Capital and life felonies and felonies resulting in death have no time limit.
What if I cannot afford a criminal defense lawyer?
You can ask the court to appoint the public defender, who represents people who cannot afford a lawyer.

family-law.lead: Florida divorce is no-fault, requires six months of residency, and presumes equal time-sharing of children unless shown otherwise.
rows: One spouse must have lived in Florida 6 months before filing (Fla. Stat. § 61.021)
At least 20 days from filing before a final judgment (§ 61.19)
Rebuttable presumption that equal time-sharing is in the child's best interests (§ 61.13)
No-fault: the marriage is irretrievably broken (§ 61.052)
faq: How long do you have to live in Florida to get divorced?
At least one spouse must have lived in Florida for 6 months before filing the petition.
Does Florida favor equal time-sharing?
Yes. Florida law presumes equal time-sharing is in the child's best interests, but a parent can rebut that by showing it is not.

immigration.lead: Immigration is federal law, decided by USCIS and the immigration courts, and only lawyers or accredited representatives may give legal advice on it.
rows: Federal immigration law, the same in every state
U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (applications) and the immigration courts of the Executive Office for Immigration Review (removal cases)
A licensed lawyer or a representative accredited by the Department of Justice (8 C.F.R. § 292.1)
Board Certification in Immigration and Nationality Law
faq: Can a notary help with my immigration case?
No. Only a licensed lawyer or a Department of Justice accredited representative may give legal advice or represent you in immigration matters.
Do I need a Florida lawyer for immigration?
Immigration law is federal, so a lawyer licensed in any U.S. state can handle it; a Florida Bar board-certified lawyer has met Florida's standards in the field.

estate-planning.lead: A Florida will must be signed in front of two witnesses, and small or older estates can use a simpler probate.
rows: Signed at the end by the testator in front of at least two witnesses, who sign in front of the testator and each other (Fla. Stat. § 732.502)
Available when the estate is $75,000 or less (excluding exempt property) or the person died more than 2 years ago (§ 735.201)
If survived by a spouse or minor child, the home can only be left to the spouse (Fla. Const. art. X, § 4)
faq: How many witnesses does a Florida will need?
Two. The person making the will signs in front of both witnesses, and the witnesses sign in front of that person and each other.
What is summary administration in Florida?
A simpler probate for estates worth $75,000 or less, not counting exempt property, or where the person died more than 2 years ago.

real-estate.lead: Florida taxes deeds at 70 cents per $100 and protects primary homes with a homestead exemption and an annual cap on assessment increases.
rows: 70 cents per $100 of the price (Fla. Stat. § 201.02)
Up to $50,000 off the assessed value of a primary residence (Fla. Const. art. VII, § 6)
Assessed value of a homestead rises by no more than 3% a year or inflation, whichever is lower (art. VII, § 4)
faq: What is the documentary stamp tax on a Florida home sale?
70 cents for every $100 of the price on the deed, under section 201.02 of the Florida Statutes.
How much does the Florida homestead exemption save?
It removes up to $50,000 from the assessed value of a primary residence, and the Save Our Homes cap limits yearly increases to 3% or inflation.
real-estate.certName: Board Certified in Real Estate Law

business-law.lead: Florida gives five years to sue on a written contract and four on an oral one.
rows: The Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act (ch. 501, part II)
faq: How long do I have to sue for breach of contract in Florida?
5 years for a written contract and 4 years for an oral one.
What does a business litigation lawyer do?
Represents companies and owners in disputes such as contract breaches, partnership and shareholder conflicts and unfair competition, in court or arbitration.

tax-law.lead: Florida has no personal income tax; it taxes corporate income at 5.5% and most sales at 6% at the state level.
rows: None; the Florida Constitution prohibits it (art. VII, § 5)
faq: Does Florida have a state income tax?
Not for individuals; the Florida Constitution bars a personal income tax. Corporations pay 5.5% on net income.
When do I need a tax lawyer?
For IRS or Florida Department of Revenue audits and disputes, tax debt, business structuring and estate tax planning.

employment-law.lead: Florida's minimum wage is $15.00 an hour, and discrimination complaints must reach the state commission within 365 days.
rows: $15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026 (Fla. Const. art. X, § 24)
Florida Civil Rights Act, employers with 15 or more employees (Fla. Stat. § 760.02)
365 days to file with the Florida Commission on Human Relations (§ 760.11)
faq: What is the minimum wage in Florida?
$15.00 per hour since September 30, 2026; from 2027 it is adjusted each year for inflation.
How long do I have to file a discrimination complaint in Florida?
365 days from the act to file with the Florida Commission on Human Relations.
employment-law.certName: Board Certified in Labor and Employment Law

elder-law.lead: Florida elder law covers guardianship, long-term care planning and powers of attorney, which must be signed before two witnesses and a notary.
rows: Signed by the principal before two witnesses and a notary (Fla. Stat. § 709.2105)
Court-supervised under chapter 744 when a person cannot manage their affairs
faq: How is a power of attorney signed in Florida?
The principal signs in front of two witnesses and a notary, under section 709.2105.
Where do I report elder abuse in Florida?
Call the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873.

workers-compensation.lead: Report a work injury to your employer within 30 days and file any petition for benefits within 2 years; lawyer fees are set by statute.
rows: Within 2 years of knowing the injury was work-related (§ 440.19)
Employers with 4 or more employees; construction employers with 1 or more (§ 440.02)
20% of the first $5,000 of benefits, 15% of the next $5,000, then 10% (5% after 10 years) (§ 440.34)
faq: How long do I have to report a work injury in Florida?
30 days from the injury or from when symptoms first appear.
How much does a workers' compensation lawyer cost in Florida?
Fees are set by law: 20% of the first $5,000 of benefits secured, 15% of the next $5,000 and 10% of the rest during the first 10 years.
